$comment: Deterministic checks that GRADE a change, by the area they cover (docs/product-reset/58, W2).
A gate must exit non-zero on failure, and must say in `meaning` what a failure tells a person.
A file matched by no gate here is UNGUARDED: a weaker model must not be trusted with it,
because nothing deterministic would catch a mistake. Adding a gate is therefore the way to
make more of the repo cheap to work on — widen the gates, do not widen the trust.
Hand-written and tracked in git on purpose; the counters beside it (usage.json) are not.

gates.meaning: Text would drop below AA contrast over the surface it is actually composited on. This is measured across 119 text nodes in both themes, windowed and full-screen — it catches what a diff cannot.
The motion tokens no longer match their generated source, so the stylesheet and the TypeScript disagree about timing.
The design-preview harness no longer builds, so every theme x window state can no longer be verified without launching Electron.
The desktop app no longer typechecks.
The engine no longer bundles. This is the check that catches a dangling import, because tsconfig excludes __tests__ and tsc therefore cannot (bimax-jest-cache-false-green).

An action Bimax claims to offer is missing from the BUILT bundle — the bimax:// URL scheme, an App Intents extension's metadata, or the engine itself. This is the repository's most-repeated failure shape: the code compiles, every other gate stays green, and macOS discovers nothing. It inspects a real .app and fails rather than skipping when there is none, because the previous packaging guard degraded to a skip and stayed green through three shipped regressions.

This machine cannot cut a signed, notarized release: a missing Developer ID certificate, missing notarization credentials, a notarize option in the wrong shape for this electron-builder, or an output directory inside an iCloud-synced tree. Every one of these otherwise surfaces minutes into a build or minutes into a failed upload. It prints no secret, only presence and shape.

engine-lint: `npm run lint` was written here as a gate and then REMOVED, because declaring it would have
been dishonest: measured 2026-09-19 it exits with 12 errors and 1,464 warnings on a clean
src/memory/facts.ts and src/tools/args.validate.ts, none of them touched by that day's work.
A gate that is ALREADY RED cannot grade a change: you cannot tell a new failure from the
standing one, so it would mark every engine file 'covered' while catching nothing, and the
escalation would fire on every turn. Fix the 12 errors, then declare it.
This is the safe direction — an undeclared area reads as unguarded, which refuses the cheap
